notes: The input is the bytes of the body of one answer of attendance. params.status is the HTTP status of that answer.
params.family, params.session and params.turns are the arguments of the entry point.
value.request is the call that the reader makes: the path, and each parameter of the query as text. The reader sends its token in a header and never in the query.
value.session is the session of the answer, as noticeboard.sessions.list gives one. value.turns is each turn of the answer.

running is true for a turn in one of the three states that are not final. usage.tokens_text is the sum of the four counts of the usage, as a page shows it. The sum of four counts of 64 bits can need more than 64 bits.
The reader takes the first 100 items of the list of turns and then drops each item that is no object.
A field of a wrong type reads as an empty text, as 0, as false or as absent. A text has 500 characters or less. A character is one code point.
A refused vector is an answer that the reader gets nothing from. refusal is the problem that a page shows.

A problem is an object. class is one of none, missing, unreadable, too large, not JSON, not an object, refused, unreachable and capped. capped is a notice: the reader stopped at a limit and kept what it read before.

text is the sentence that a page shows. A problem of the class not JSON has no text: its sentence ends with a message of the JSON reader of Python. It has start, the part of the sentence before that message.

refusal.text: attendance's answer is list, not a JSON object
attendance's answer is NoneType, not a JSON object
